title: Osso Buco
description: Cross-cut veal shanks braised slowly in white wine and tomato until the marrow softens, finished with a sharp gremolata of lemon, garlic, and parsley.
notes: Ask the butcher for hind shanks — they are meatier than the fore. Serve with risotto alla milanese or soft polenta, and a small spoon each for the marrow.

steps.text: Tie each veal shank around its circumference with string so the meat stays on the bone, then season and dust lightly with the flour.
steps.tip: Snip the membrane around the edge in two or three places as well, or it contracts in the heat and the shank curls up in the pan.

steps.text: Brown the shanks in the olive oil on both flat sides, then set aside.
Lower the heat, add the butter, and soften the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble until reduced by half.
Add the tomatoes, stock, and bay leaf, return the shanks in a single layer, cover, and braise very gently until the meat is yielding.
steps.tip: They should sit no more than halfway submerged. Turn them once, halfway through, so the tops do not dry out.

steps.text: Chop the parsley with the garlic and lemon zest until fine.
Lift out the shanks, snip off the string, and reduce the sauce if it is thin. Spoon it over and scatter the gremolata just before serving.
steps.tip: Gremolata goes on at the table, raw. Stirred into the pot it loses the brightness that is its whole job.
